messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for model-redwood-2-large in us-west-2 — p99 gen latency crossed 3.2s for the last 5m, streaming stall rate increased. Pager severity: P2.
adebayo: Oncall here. I'm pulling logs now, give me 30s. @maria can you confirm if there were any recent deploys to the runtime?
maria: No deploys in the past hour from eng-runtime. Seeing a cluster-level spike in tail latency for GPU-backed pods.
sophia: I can see multiple GPUs with rising ECC corrected counts on nvml for node gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-15. Also thermal alarm messages ~10:21UTC.
linus: Thanks. Is traffic concentrated to a specific AZ/selector? k8s shows these nodes in us-west-2a serving model-redwood-2-large.
adebayo: Confirmed. 85% of p99 traces route to a handful of pods on node gpu-node-12. Those pods' containers have streaming keepalive stalls.
infra-bot: NOTE: GPU node gpu-node-12 reported nvml: ECC_CORRECTION_STATS increase (last sample +4k corrections), fan RPM spike, and GPU clock throttling events.
adebayo: Ok, immediate plan: 1) Drain affected node(s) 2) Fail traffic to fallback model variant (cpu-quantized) for new sessions 3) Notify customers if impact > 5% error/latency.
maria: Start draining now. Command I'll run: ```rctl node cordon gpu-node-12 && rctl drain gpu-node-12 --grace-period=60 --evict-local=false```
sophia: While draining, set routing policy to prefer us-west-2b/c capacity and enable automatic fallback to model-redwood-2-small for streaming sessions > 5s. I can flip the routing flag.
linus: I pushed a temporary queueing throttle on the ingress to limit inflight streams per user to 20 to avoid amplification.
adebayo: infra-bot, can you confirm if Dedicated pool has spare capacity for immediate burst?
infra-bot: Dedicated pool us-west-2 has 15% free GPU capacity. Autoscaler shows 2 nodes can be spun within ~4 minutes.
jason: Support: already seeing explanations from a few customers about increased latency. Opening a customer-impact tracker now. I'll post updates to support channel and set banner.
sophia: Draining started, pods are terminating; some are stuck in Terminating state due to long streaming sessions. I'll force-evict after 60s if they don't close gracefully.
maria: Here's a snippet from node logs showing NVML events: ```[10:20:41 UTC] GPU0 ECC_CORRECTABLE 4123 -> 4137; [10:21:12 UTC] THERMAL_GOV: throttle_enter; [10:21:45 UTC] FAN_RPM spike 4500->7800```
adebayo: Good evidence of hardware-induced throttling. We'll mark gpu-node-12 as quarantined and open a hardware ticket with provider.
linus: After routing changes, p95 improved to ~420ms, but p99 still at 1.9s due to long-tail streams. We're avoiding hitting SLO at 99.9% but p99 is still borderline.
sophia: I'm enabling KV-prefix caching for common prompt prefixes in the affected model for the next 10m to reduce re-compute on cold starts. This should cut tail tokens by ~20-30%.
aadeb? (typo) -- ignore
jason: Customer banner posted: "We are aware of intermittent increased latency affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating." Replied to 3 priority customers.
adebayo: Any errors beyond latency? We saw few 503s early on.
maria: A handful of sessions returned stalled streams with keepalive drop; those are from pods that didn't gracefully close due to GPU stall. No broad 5xx surge.
infra-bot: Autoscaler: starting 2 nodes (est ready 4m). Current draining progress: 6/8 pods evacuated from gpu-node-12.
sophia: Force-evicted remaining 2 long-lived streams (they were idle but stuck); restarted their sessions into fallback model.
linus: Observability: added a temporary trace tag to mark routed fallback flows so we can measure quality regressions. Dashboard updated.
jason: Support will send a targeted email to affected customers if we can't restore baseline in 30m.
adebayo: OK handoff plan: I'm going to escalate to oncall-handoff rotation in 25m. If p99 < 1.2s and no new ECC spikes, we can close active mitigation and continue monitoring. Otherwise escalate to hardware vendor.
maria: Node quarantined and hardware ticket created: HT-98765 (GPU ECC/thermal anomaly, gpu-node-12). Pls add any request context there.
sophia: Quick note: model-quality alert suppressed for fallback routing to avoid eval noise. I'll re-enable once routing is back to normal.
infra-bot: Event: node gpu-node-12 state=QUARANTINED; ticket=HT-98765; autoscaler nodes_in_progress=2.
adebayo: Thanks team. Last checks: p95 390ms, p99 1.0s, streaming stall rate down 85% vs peak. Switching to monitoring mode. @jason please keep customers updated. I'll hand off to next oncall in 25m with notes here. :thumbsup:
jason: Will do. Posting update in support and incident channels.
support-bot: Automated note: incident page created https://redwood.incidents/5468799999 — severity P2, status: mitigated -> monitoring.
linus: Leaving a follow-up action item: run postmortem focusing on GPU lifetime ECC patterns and preemptive eviction thresholds.
adebayo: Handoff: next oncall is maria (next shift). I'm tagging the incident and leaving runbook link. ```/runbook incident/gpu-throttle```. If anything regresses ping @pagerduty.
maria: Acknowledged. I'll own post-incident and coordinate hardware RMA if needed.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (drain/quarantine/fallback routing). Monitoring for 60m.
adebayo: closing active coordination here, moving to incident doc. Thanks all."
